column3: “A great help” renders the personal title patroness or benefactor.
“Risked their lives” renders the image of laying down their own neck for his life.
“Household” supplies the group implied by those of Aristobulus.
“Fellow countryman” specifies kinsman; “household” supplies the group implied by those of Narcissus.
The first two women's labor is present in the Greek; “my” is supplied before beloved Persis.
“And mine” is expanded as having been a mother to him as well.
Their obedience reaching everyone is made explicit as everyone having heard about it.
BSB’s “Christ” in the blessing matches the Textus Receptus (Χριστοῦ); the critical text has “our Lord Jesus.”
“Treasurer” specifies steward; “our” is supplied before brother.
This verse is absent from the critical text, and BSB omits it; the Textus Receptus repeats the blessing “The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.”
“To lead” and “comes from” make the relation between the nations, obedience, and faith explicit.
